Spina bifida (myelomeningocele)

No animal evidence was identified in the mapped clinical categories.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

No animal evidence was identified in the mapped clinical categories.

Summary of the Evidence

Four publications are mapped across Development > Spina bifida and Surgery > Myelomeningocele repair. They represent two likely patient cohorts: a pediatric rehabilitation trial and a neonatal surgical cohort. One publication is the protocol for the later randomized trial, and two neonatal reports appear to describe the same patients rather than independent cohorts.

Human and clinical evidence

Silva et al. conducted a randomized rehabilitation trial with 25 children enrolled and 20 completing the protocol. Physiotherapy plus PBM was compared with physiotherapy plus sham; both groups improved in functional mobility and muscle electrical activity, but there was no significant between-group advantage for PBM (2023). The earlier protocol describes the same planned study and should not be counted as a second trial (Silva et al. 2021). Pinto et al. reported a 13-neonate pilot compared with 23 historical non-laser controls. Incision dehiscence was reported in 7.69% versus 17.39%, but nonrandomized historical comparison and the small sample make the estimate uncertain (2010). Two neonatal titles appear to report this same cohort.

Animal evidence

No animal study was identified in these mapped clinical records.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The rehabilitation intervention was paired with physiotherapy and compared with sham PBM, so it tests an added treatment effect under that program. The neonatal report used 685-nm light at 21 mW and 0.19 J per point, with 4–10 J per infant. Differences in age, surgery, treatment purpose, and outcome prevent generalizing one protocol to the other.

Interpretation

The randomized rehabilitation study did not show a significant added functional benefit. A small historical-control neonatal signal is not sufficient to establish wound protection.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for added functional benefit in children with myelomeningocele Very low for reducing neonatal wound dehiscence
Publications and records4 publications representing 2 likely cohorts.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Four titles represent a rehabilitation trial, its protocol, and two reports of one small neonatal cohort. The rehabilitation trial found no significant added PBM effect over physiotherapy, while the neonatal reports used historical controls and are likely overlapping. Larger prospective studies should separate functional and wound outcomes.

Publication and study types

  • Human1 randomized rehabilitation trial report plus its protocol; 2 neonatal reports likely describe the same 13 infants, compared with historical controls.
  • No animal or standalone in-vitro study.
  • Do not count the protocol or duplicate neonatal report as an independent cohort.
